effective_source.effect: A font dictionary carries information that can be used to provide a substitute when the font program is not available; embedded font programs are optional. This permits a substitute and does not prescribe one for a supplied but malformed program.
effective_source.primary_locator: Effective EC3 primary physical 326 / printed 311; processed text line 7627-7630.

effective_source.effect: Descriptor metrics provide information enabling a processor to synthesize or select a similar font when the program is unavailable. No mandatory malformed-program fallback algorithm appears in this checked passage.
effective_source.primary_locator: Effective EC3 primary physical 358 / printed 343; processed text line 8342-8348.

effective_source.effect: Defines recognized embedded program organizations and stream entries including Length1/2/3. These producer format/extent requirements establish why bad bytes may be refused; they do not require a particular reader recovery when parsing fails.
effective_source.primary_locator: §9.9.1 header confirmed; Table 125 is effective EC3 primary physical 368 / printed 353; processed text line 8529-8566.

implementation.behavior: Only FontError::Malformed for a program stream already supplied and read reaches this recovery. It drops the three program keys from a copied descriptor and follows the absent-program substitute route. It excludes NO_CODE_REACHES_A_GLYPH, a readable program whose encoding reaches no glyph. The caller retains and reports the originating refusal; the public interpretation remains incomplete.

assertions.quality: Strong exact-xref public control: same host, font dictionary and page text, with FontFile2 absent in one PDF and unreadable bytes in the other; asserts no recovery, identical raster/text/origins, two visible glyphs, independent second origin 10 + 667/1000 * 36 = 34.012, refusal retained and incomplete status. This closes the earlier durable T11 coverage gap.

assertions.quality: Additional selected simple/composite outcomes, reporting, no-route and forbidden-Identity controls, plus corpus witnesses. Existing source comments note these handcrafted fixtures do not all use exact xrefs; the new paired audit test is the independent exact-xref behavior control. Composite substitute coverage is conditional on machine-addressable substitute availability.

Broad present-file consumer sweep with per-document pixels/report expectations; only the two PDFIUM-407 expectations above conflict with the newly accepted recovery policy. Not a normative conformance oracle for malformed producer files.

verdict: ADR 2870 remains a current, owner-ratified recovery policy under A837, not a reader obligation imposed by §§9.5/9.8.1. The actual code preserves the malformed-program refusal while visibly substituting and correctly excludes readable-but-unmapped program behavior. The parent-reported fixed-documents failure is a stale ratchet limited to PDFIUM-407-0.pdf and should be reconciled in the gate expectations; no new behavior test is needed because the exact-xref paired-control assertion already exists and has passed in parent review.
residuals: No claim that a malformed embedded font must be substituted under ISO; exact recovery remains product policy.
D51 requires a reviewed replacement for the obsolete expectations; do not simply copy observed ink14.633 into a new golden band. Three refusal reports should remain observable under accepted policy.
This review does not certify every malformed font format or every composite substitute route.
